caption: The drawing is on a wooden shield-shaped plaque with a worn, weathered appearance and is primarily brown and gray in color. Across the top of the shield, the name "H. ROSE." is written in large, uppercase letters. The left side of the shield features the brown silhouettes of trees, and on the right side is a full-length figure of a person in black clothing and a black top hat, facing left, holding a reddish-brown bird on their outstretched hand. Behind the figure, there is more brown shading that suggests land or ground. Across the midsection of the shield, following a curved path, is the faint inscription: "A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush." The lower portion of the shield contains a light gray outline of a square and compasses, a symbol often associated with Freemasonry, on the unpainted wood background that shows stains and signs of age.
title: Tavern Sign
